picks.title: "We got this wrong… We do not support AI-generated music": D'Addario admits generative AI was used on string demo video after all
picks.excerpt: D'Addario reversed its denial and confirmed Suno Studio was used to "regenerate the original track" in its NYXL HD electric guitar string demo video. The brand apologised for sharing inaccurate information and for deleting critical comments, and says its process will change going forward.
picks.rationale: A major instrument brand gets caught denying generative AI in its own marketing audio — the clearest signal yet that undisclosed AI in a demo is now a reputational liability, not a shortcut.

picks.title: OMNi (alpha v0.1), a FREE Rust-based DAW with native AI sample generation
picks.excerpt: Developer Tomasz Głuc has released OMNi, a free DAW written entirely in Rust with AI sample generation and image-to-sound synthesis built into the core rather than bolted on as a plugin. It's an early alpha, but it points at what a natively generative DAW looks like.
picks.rationale: The first free DAW where generation lives in the core instead of a plugin slot — downloadable today and the closest look at how a natively generative session actually behaves.

picks.title: Suno announces vinyl pressing service for AI-generated music
picks.excerpt: Suno users can now compile tracks from their library into a custom 12-inch record holding up to 46 minutes of audio, pressed and shipped by Suno for around $45 plus shipping. It pushes prompt-generated music into a physical, collectible format for the first time.
picks.rationale: Prompt-generated music gets a physical release format and a price — a new distribution surface, and a packaging/artwork problem landing on designers' desks.

picks.title: Push Hack, very unauthorized access to Push 3's display, files, MIDI, and more
picks.excerpt: Federico Pepe's Push Hack opens SSH access to Ableton Push 3's Linux layer, giving full control of the display, file system and MIDI routing. Notably, it was built with AI-assisted coding agents — a reminder that machine learning is now very good at reverse-engineering closed music hardware.
picks.rationale: Coding agents cracked a closed controller's firmware and handed users its display and MIDI layer — the practical proof that AI is now a hardware-modding tool, not just a sound generator.

picks.title: Sonarworks expand SoundID VoiceAI library
picks.excerpt: Sonarworks added a C-Pop Voices Expansion Pack of 10 Chinese voice models to SoundID VoiceAI, aimed at Mandopop and Cantopop production. The models were trained on ethically sourced material with artist consent and compensation.
picks.rationale: Licensed, consent-and-royalty voice models keep expanding by language and market — the cleanest working example of vocal AI that a commercial release can actually clear.
